arxiv-2002-06296.title: Sparse Coresets for SVD on Infinite Streams
arxiv-2002-06296.creator: Vladimir Braverman, Dan Feldman, Harry Lang, Daniela Rus, Adiel Statman
arxiv-2002-06296.description: Abstract In streaming Singular Value Decomposition (SVD), d d -dimensional rows of a possibly infinite matrix arrive sequentially as points in ℝ d \mathbb{R}^{d} . An ϵ \epsilon -coreset is a (much smaller) matrix whose sum of square distances of the rows to any hyperplane approximates that of the original matrix to a 1 ± ϵ 1\pm\epsilon factor.

arxiv-2003-08985.title: An atlas of K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group
arxiv-2003-08985.creator: Xavier Roulleau
arxiv-2003-08985.description: Abstract Abstract. We study the geometry of K3 surfaces with finite automorphism group and Picard number at least 3 . We describe these surfaces classified by Nikulin and Vinberg as double covers of simpler surfaces or as embedded in a projective space. We study, moreover, the configurations of their finite set of (-2) -curves. Keywords.

arxiv-2005-04442.title: Null controllability for the singular heat equation with a memory term
arxiv-2005-04442.creator: Brahim Allal Faculté des Sciences et TechniquesUniversité Hassan 1er, Laboratoire MISI,B.P. 577, Settat 26000, Moroccoemail: b.allal@uhp.ac.ma Genni Fragnelli Dipartimento di MatematicaUniversità di Bari Aldo MoroVia E. Orabona 470125 Bari - Italyemail: genni.fragnelli@uniba.it Jawad Salhi Faculté d
arxiv-2005-04442.description: Abstract In this paper we focus on the null controllability problem for the heat equation with the so-called inverse square potential and a memory term. To this aim, we first establish the null controllability for a nonhomogeneous singular heat equation by a new Carleman inequality with weights which do not blow up at t = 0 t=0 .

arxiv-2108-04491.title: New opportunites for interactions and control with ultracold lanthanides
arxiv-2108-04491.creator: Matthew A. Norcia, Francesca Ferlaino
arxiv-2108-04491.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Matthew A. Norcia, Francesca Ferlaino. Lanthanide atoms have an unusual electron configuration, with a partially filled shell of f f orbitals. This leads to a set of characteristic properties that enable enhanced control over ultracold atoms and their interactions: large numbers of optical transitions with widely varying wavelengths and transition strengths, anisotropic interaction properties between atoms and with light, and a large magnetic moment and spin space present in the ground state.

arxiv-2111-04080.title: Cross-modal Zero-shot Hashing by Label Attributes Embedding
arxiv-2111-04080.creator: Runmin Wang, Guoxian Yu, Lei Liu, Lizhen Cui, Carlotta Domeniconi, Xiangliang Zhang
arxiv-2111-04080.description: Abstract Cross-modal hashing (CMH) is one of the most promising methods in cross-modal approximate nearest neighbor search. Most CMH solutions ideally assume the labels of training and testing set are identical. However, the assumption is often violated, causing a zero-shot CMH problem.

arxiv-2201-13291.title: Metrics for saliency map evaluation of deep learning explanation methods Thanks: Supported by Nantes Excellence Trajectory (NExT)
arxiv-2201-13291.creator: Tristan Gomez, Thomas Fréour, Harold Mouchère
arxiv-2201-13291.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tristan Gomez, Thomas Fréour, Harold Mouchère. Due to the black-box nature of deep learning models, there is a recent development of solutions for visual explanations of CNNs. Given the high cost of user studies, metrics are necessary to compare and evaluate these different methods. In this paper, we critically analyze the Deletion Area Under Curve (DAUC) and Insertion Area Under Curve (IAUC) metrics proposed by Petsiuk et al.

arxiv-2301-00319.title: Quantum Hairy Black Hole Formation and Horizon Quantum Mechanics
arxiv-2301-00319.creator: R. T. Cavalcanti, J. M. Hoff da Silva
arxiv-2301-00319.description: Abstract After introducing the gravitational decoupling method and the hairy black hole recently derived from it, we investigate the formation of quantum hairy black holes by applying the horizon quantum mechanics formalism. It enables us to determine how external fields, characterized by hairy parameters, affect the probability of spherically symmetric black hole formation and the generalized uncertainty principle.

arxiv-2311-07960.title: Flat Connections from Irregular Conformal Blocks
arxiv-2311-07960.creator: Babak Haghighat, Yihua Liu, and Nicolai Reshetikhin
arxiv-2311-07960.description: Abstract In this work we study Liouville conformal blocks with degenerate primaries and one operator in an irregular representation of the Virasoro algebra. Using an algebraic approach, we derive modified BPZ equations satisfied by such blocks and subsequently construct corresponding integral representations based on integration over non-compact Lefschetz cycles.

arxiv-2408-03572.title: 2D-OOB: Attributing Data Contribution Through Joint Valuation Framework
arxiv-2408-03572.creator: Yifan Sun, Jingyan Shen *, Yongchan Kwon
arxiv-2408-03572.description: Abstract Data valuation has emerged as a powerful framework for quantifying each datum’s contribution to the training of a machine learning model. However, it is crucial to recognize that the quality of cells within a single data point can vary greatly in practice. For example, even in the case of an abnormal data point, not all cells are necessarily noisy.

arxiv-2412-13091.title: LMUnit : Fine-grained Evaluation with Natural Language Unit Tests
arxiv-2412-13091.creator: Jon Saad-Falcon 1,2 , Rajan Vivek 1* , William Berrios 1* Nandita Shankar Naik 1 , Matija Franklin 1 , Bertie Vidgen 1 Amanpreet Singh 1 , Douwe Kiela 1,2 , Shikib Mehri 1 1 Contextual AI 2 Stanford University, Department of Computer Science jonsaadfalcon@stanford.edu , shikib@contextual.ai
arxiv-2412-13091.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jon Saad-Falcon 1,2 , Rajan Vivek 1* , William Berrios 1* Nandita Shankar Naik 1 , Matija Franklin 1 , Bertie Vidgen 1 Amanpreet Singh 1 , Douwe Kiela 1,2 , Shikib Mehri 1 1 Contextual AI 2 Stanford University, Department of Computer Science jonsaadfalcon@stanford.edu , shikib@contextual.ai. As language models become integral to critical workflows, assessing their behavior remains a fundamental challenge – human evaluation is costly and noisy, while automated metrics provide only coarse, difficult-to-interpret signals.

arxiv-2505-14301.title: Efficient direct loading of the green MOT of Yb with low green laser power
arxiv-2505-14301.creator: Thilagaraj Ravi, Rajnandan Choudhury Das, Heramb Vivek Bhusane, Samrat Roy, Kanhaiya Pandey
arxiv-2505-14301.description: Abstract We report the direct loading of Ytterbium (Yb) atoms in the magneto-optical trap (MOT) using the intercombination narrow optical transition 6s 2 1 S 0 → \rightarrow 6s6p 3 P 1 at 556 nm (green), known as green MOT with limited power of green laser, 10 mW.

arxiv-2507-18761.title: Freezeout at constant energy density and spin polarization in heavy-ion collisions
arxiv-2507-18761.creator: Andrea Palermo, Masoud Shokri
arxiv-2507-18761.description: Abstract Using the local equilibrium density operator, we develop a geometry-informed linear response theory that takes into account the parameterization of the freezeout hypersurface before the gradient expansion is carried out. Assuming local equilibrium on an iso-energy density hypersurface, we study the Λ \Lambda hyperon spin polarization, and compute corrections to the isothermal case due to finite density.

arxiv-2602-12130.title: On minimal pattern-containing inversion sequences
arxiv-2602-12130.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by . We introduce the notion of minimal inversion sequences for a pattern ρ \rho , which form the smallest set of inversion sequences whose avoidance is equivalent to the avoidance of ρ \rho for inversion sequences. We give a characterization of ρ \rho -minimal inversion sequences based on the occurrences of the pattern ρ \rho they contain, and use it to find upper and lower bounds on the lengths of ρ \rho -minimal inversion sequences.

pmc-10476288.title: Integrating intimate partner violence prevention content into a digital parenting chatbot intervention during COVID-19: Intervention development and remote data collection
pmc-10476288.creator: Moa Schafer, Jamie M Lachman, Frances Gardner, Paula Zinser, Francisco Calderon, Qing Han, Chiara Facciola, Lily Clements
pmc-10476288.description: BackgroundIntimate partner violence (IPV) is a serious public health issue which experienced a sharp incline during the onset of COVID-19. Increases in other forms of violence, such as violence against children (VAC), have also been linked to the pandemic, and there have been calls for greater prevention efforts that tackle both forms of violence concurrently.

pmc-10698949.title: Targeting the host response in sepsis: current approaches and future evidence
pmc-10698949.creator: Christian Bode, Sebastian Weis, Andrea Sauer, Pedro Wendel-Garcia, Sascha David
pmc-10698949.description: Sepsis, a dysregulated host response to infection characterized by organ failure, is one of the leading causes of death worldwide. Disbalances of the immune response play an important role in its pathophysiology. Patients may develop simultaneously or concomitantly states of systemic or local hyperinflammation and immunosuppression.

pmc-13045951.title: Fatal complication from Foley’s catheter: a case report
pmc-13045951.creator: Huda Meshikhes, Abdullah Waheeb, Omar Baasim, Ali AlAbbad, Riyad Al Mousa, Ali AlZahar
pmc-13045951.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Introduction and importance:Foley’s catheterization is a common and routinely performed procedure, yet it carries risks including urinary tract infection, urethral trauma, and, more rarely, bladder perforation. Reports of simultaneous bladder and bowel injury during catheter exchange are exceedingly uncommon.Case presentation:We report an 86-year-old woman with hypertension, heart failure, and a history of uterine cancer treated with chemotherapy and pelvic radiotherapy 2 decades earlier. After a routine Foley’s catheter exchange, she developed paraumbilical pain and decreased urine output.

pmc-13346942.title: Freeze–thaw performance of self-compacting concrete with GGBFS, fly ash and limestone powder: linking strength loss to air-void parameters
pmc-13346942.creator: Tomasz Rudnicki, Piotr Smarzewski
pmc-13346942.description: Comparative evidence on how different supplementary cementitious materials affect freeze–thaw performance and air-void system characteristics of self-compacting concrete (SCC) under consistent mixture conditions remains limited. This study provides a direct comparative assessment of ground granulated blast-furnace slag (GGBFS), fly ash (FA), and limestone powder (LM) as partial cement replacements in SCC within a unified mix-design framework.

pmc-13393346.description: and systemic immunosuppressive therapies, including oral corticosteroids, doxycycline, and steroid-sparing agents.1 However, many patients experience refractory disease, steroid dependence, or treatment-limiting adverse effects. pmc-13578141.title: Tailor-Made Nanoporous Metal–Organic Frameworks Via Molecular Engineering for Bilirubin-Specific Capture from Liver Failure Patients’ Blood
pmc-13578141.creator: Shanshan Zhang, Jinming Zhang, Yihan Li, Dabao Shang, Ding Zhao, Fangke Zhang, Juan Wang, Liang Chen, Xiaogang Xiang, Wenguo Cui
pmc-13578141.description: Hightlights This work innovatively formulated a molecular engineering strategy for nanoframeworks, achieving precise customization of their nanoporous architectures.This work developed a nanoscale bilirubin-specific capture trap, physically overcoming the critical trade-off between bilirubin removal and protein loss. A groundbreaking 251% increase in total bilirubin capture capacity, coupled with an albumin loss rate of ≤2.58%, established a new world clinical assessment record.
